t: This is a terrace of houses in Westminster, taking in one to four Suffolk Place, twenty-three Suffolk Street and three Haymarket. The design is by John Nash, the Georgian and Regency architect who shaped many important areas of London. His neoclassical and picturesque work was paid for by the Prince Regent and by the developer James Burton. Nash also collaborated extensively with Burton's son, Decimus Burton. So as you stand at this corner, you're looking at one small part of Nash's much larger legacy across the capital.
